author: Linnaeus, 1758
habitat: 번식지: 다른 새의 빈 둥지, 나무구멍, 절벽과 바위 틈
summary: 전국에 찾아오지만 흔하지 않은 겨울철새다. 둥지를 스스로 짓지 않고 까마귀류 같은 다른 새의 빈 둥지나 나무구멍, 절벽, 바위 틈에 알 3~6개를 낳는다. 북위 40°에서 북극에 이르는 유럽, 아시아, 북아메리카에 분포하며, 한국, 일본, 중국, 이란, 이집트 등지에서 겨울을 난다.

points.en: broad black band at the tail tip (male)

points.ko: 옅은 갈색 바탕에 적갈색 줄무늬 배(암컷)

sexes.male: 등이 회색이고 꼬리 끝에 넓은 검은 띠가 있으며, 배에 연한 적갈색 줄무늬가 있다.
sexes.female: 등이 갈색이고 옅은 갈색 배에 적갈색 줄무늬가 있으며, 꼬리에는 갈색 줄무늬가 있다.

art.subject: Merlin (Falco columbarius), adult male in Korean winter (October–March): crown, back, wings and tail blue-grey, the crown finely streaked black; faint whitish supercilium and only a thin, weak dark moustachial line; indistinct rufous-buff nape collar; cheeks and throat whitish; underparts orange-buff to pale rufous, boldly streaked dark brown on the breast, belly and flanks; tail blue-grey with a broad black band near the tip and a narrow white tip. Short hooked bill bluish-grey with a dark tip; cere, eye-ring and legs yellow; dark brown eye.
art.pose: perched upright on a low wooden post in open farmland, scanning for small birds, side view
art.scene: Korean winter open farmland: harvested rice paddies with straw stubble, earth levees and a low wooden post, bare trees in the distance, clear cold light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched on a post: blue-grey crown, back and wings, rufous-buff nape collar, orange-buff underparts streaked dark brown, blue-grey tail with a broad black subterminal band and white tip, yellow cere and legs

adult female, side view perched: dark brown upperparts, pale buff supercilium, whitish to buff underparts heavily streaked rufous-brown, brown tail crossed by several narrow pale buff bands and a darker band near the tip
art.build: Small, compact falcon, 28–33cm long, smaller and stockier than Eurasian Kestrel and about the length of a feral pigeon; female clearly larger than the male. Broad-chested, with a rounded head and a short, deep, hooked bill. Wings fairly short, broad-based and sharply pointed; at rest the wingtips fall clearly short of the tail tip. Tail medium length, square-ended. Legs short and yellow. Flies fast and low with rapid, flicking wingbeats, often hugging the ground; rarely hovers.
avoid: Do not paint a rufous back with black spots and a long tail — that is Eurasian Kestrel (Falco tinnunculus).
Do not give it a bold black moustache and a blackish hood — that is Peregrine Falcon.
Do not paint broad rounded wings, barred underparts or a yellow eye like a sparrowhawk.
Do not paint the male with brown upperparts; adult males are blue-grey above.
